posts.body_html:
Sorry for the late reply! After a good season of observations, now I'm starting to have a strong suspicion as to why there are so many reports of variegation not being stable: in other words, people will find one trap with a variegated leaf and then the plant doesn't consistently produce variegated leaves after that. I believe this is because the mutation is localized (see previous page on this thread for details).

As expected, the original seedling pushed out one or two more variegated leaves, while the rest were normal. Pics taken 11/14/20:even if this clone wasn't variegated, it's still stand out, shape-wise!




Check out the side shoots: hard to tell from the photo, but only one of out several side shoots are variegated:


The one side shoot that turned out variegated is STABLE! Yesssssssssssssssssssss!!!!!! Every single trap that it pushes out is variegated. It was hard as EF to get a pic cuz the traps are so small, but you can sorta see the variegation in this photo:


With bigger traps next year, I think I'll be able to get better photos, so stay tuned!
